Ship a two-row footer, native scrollback and the macOS stdin probe

The footer is two rows again. Row 1 leads with the session title and the
permission badge (`● <title> ｜ <permission>`, falling back to `model ｜ effort`
until the session has a title); row 2 leads with `provider: model @ effort` and

quietest figures first (average, cache hit, current), then falls back to the bare

two decimals, and the footer follows the interface language at last.

bundle vendors its own patched copy), shows the DeepSeek balance next to the
session cost, and lets a sandbox-escalation prompt be self-reviewed against a

Add the tag-driven release pipeline and stop the CI flakes

.github/workflows/release.yml builds the release candidates on every v* tag
(checks, build:packages, release:hub, verify:hub), uploads them, and hands them
to a second job that publishes in the documented order — bundle, Hub profile,
launcher — behind the `release` environment. A manual dispatch publishes only
when asked, a tag that disagrees with package.json fails before anything is
published, and the npm/Hub credentials come from the NPM_PUBLISH_TOKEN and
DSH_HUB_TOKEN secrets. checks.yml cancels superseded runs on the same ref.

Both flakes seen on main are fixed: the session-messaging fixture polls for
fifteen seconds under a sixty-second guard and names the wait that expired, and
the launcher lifecycle fixture stops reporting its stub runtime ready before the
stub can take SIGTERM.

Verified: unit, ui, integration and package suites, plus a YAML parse of both
workflows.

Stop the login runtime fixture from failing on Node's one-shot exit race

The release dry run surfaced it: a one-shot Host whose work finishes fast can
drain its event loop before dsh's dispose settles, so `bin.js` ends on an
unsettled top-level await and Node exits 13 even though the plugin asked for 0.
The fixture now still requires its marker and accepts 13 only together with
Node's own warning; twelve local runs pass where two used to fail.

Also verified the rest of the gates: unit, ui, integration and package suites.

Stop the bundle from depending on a path inside itself

`file:vendor/subprocess` looked like the way to ship the patched macOS stdin
inspector, but pnpm resolves `file:` against the profile root, so every Hub
install failed with ERR_PNPM_LINKED_PKG_DIR_NOT_FOUND — the release pipeline's
verify:hub step caught it before anything was published. The dependency, the
extra vendor stage entry and the package-check assertions are gone; a build tree
without the package now warns instead of failing, and the changelog says plainly
that the probe reaches repository installs only until it moves into a package the
bundle already vendors (dsh-terminal-bash is the candidate).

Verified: unit 162/162, test:package green with the warning.

Review workspaces outside Git from a task snapshot

no_repository everywhere else, so the eval's /app tasks never called it. Outside a
Git repository dscode now snapshots the workspace as a tree in a shadow bare

files and files over 4 MiB; a workspace over 20,000 files or 256 MiB returns
no_baseline. The baseline is a ref per session, so it survives a resume, and a new
task replaces it. Without a git executable nothing changes.
